extracted.intended_audience: Owners/operators of bulk gasoline terminals, bulk gasoline plants, pipeline breakout stations, and pipeline pumping stations (facilities subject to this EPA subpart)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements for inspections, performance testing, recordkeeping, and reporting for facilities loading gasoline cargo tanks and operating vapor control/monitoring systems under the cited EPA subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: External floating roof inspection requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If your gasoline storage tank is equipped with an external floating roof, you must perform inspections of the floating roof system according to the requirements of § 60.113b(b) if complying with option 2(d) in table 1 to this subpart, or according to § 63.1063(c)(2) if complying with option 2(e) in table 1 to this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closed vent system and control device testing and monitored parameter
rubrics_metrics.description: If your gasoline storage tank is equipped with a closed vent system and control device, conduct a performance test and determine a monitored operating parameter value as required in paragraphs (a) through (d) of this section, except that the applicable level of control shall be a 95-percent reduction in inlet TOC levels rather than 80 mg/l of gasoline loaded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual certification test for gasoline cargo tanks — EPA Method 27 parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual certification test for gasoline cargo tanks shall consist of the test methods specified in paragraph (g)(1) or (2); EPA Method 27 (appendix A-8 to part 60) must be conducted using a time period of 5 minutes for the pressure and vacuum tests, initial pressure Pi = 460 mm (18 in) water gauge, initial vacuum Vi = 150 mm (6 in) water gauge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum allowable pressure/vacuum changes (Δp, Δv) for all affected gasoline cargo tanks is 3 inches of water or less in 5 minutes, unless superseded by values in column 3 of table 2 in § 63.425(e) after dates in § 63.11083.

rubrics_metrics.name: Railcar bubble leak test alternative for cargo tanks
rubrics_metrics.description: As an alternative to the annual certification test, owners/operators of railcar cargo tanks may comply with specified railcar periodic testing and bubble leak test procedures provided the railcar meets paragraph (g)(2)(iii) conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must comply with 49 CFR 173.31(d), 179.7, 180.509, and 180.511 for periodic testing; leakage pressure test per 49 CFR 180.509(j) used to show no indication of leakage per 49 CFR 180.511(f) shall be a bubble leak test meeting requirements in 49 CFR 179.7, 180.505, and 180.509. Use of ASTM E515-95 (Reapproved 2000) or BS EN 1593:1999 complies. Cannot be used for railcars that collect gasoline vapors from a vapor balance system that complies with an applicable rule or permit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative pressure monitoring during performance tests
rubrics_metrics.description: As an alternative to the pressure monitoring requirements in § 60.504a(d), you may comply with § 60.503(d) during any performance test or performance evaluation conducted under § 63.11092(e) to demonstrate compliance with § 60.502a(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance test conditions and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance tests must be conducted under conditions the Administrator specifies based on representative performance (normal operating conditions) of the affected source; tests must be conducted under representative conditions when liquid product is being loaded into gasoline cargo tanks and include periods between cargo tank loadings, provided liquid product loading occurs for at least a portion of each 5-minute block.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may not conduct performance tests during periods of malfunction. You must record process information necessary to document operating conditions during the test and include an explanation supporting that such conditions represent normal operation. Make records available to the Administrator upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of Performance Test/Performance Evaluation prior to testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Each owner/operator of an affected bulk gasoline terminal must submit a Notification of Performance Test or Performance Evaluation, as specified in subpart A, prior to initiating testing required by this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission format for Notification of Compliance Status reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner/operator must submit all Notification of Compliance Status reports in PDF format to the EPA following the procedure in § 63.9(k), except any medium submitted through mail must be sent to the attention of the Gasoline Distribution Sector Lead.

rubrics_metrics.name: General recordkeeping retention rules for storage vessel control options
rubrics_metrics.description: If complying with options 2(a), 2(b), or 2(d) in table 1, keep records as specified in § 60.115b except records shall be kept for at least 5 years. If complying with option 2(e), keep records as specified in § 63.1065.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEL monitoring event recordkeeping (options 2(c) or 2(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: If complying with options 2(c) or 2(f) in table 1, keep records of each LEL monitoring event as specified in paragraphs (a)(2)(i) through (ix) for at least 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required LEL monitoring event records: (i) date/time and storage vessel being monitored; (ii) description of monitoring event (e.g., concurrent with visual inspection, off-date, re-monitoring due to wind/repair); (iii) wind speed at top of vessel on date; (iv) LEL meter manufacturer/model and tubing type/length if used; (v) calibration checks before/after measurements including span check and instrumental offset, calibration gas used, Certificate of Analysis, results, and corrective actions for failed checks; (vi) location of measurements and floating roof location; (vii) each measurement taken at least every 15 seconds including indication of automatic correction or raw and corrected values and correction factor; (viii) each 5-minute rolling average reading; (ix) if vapor concentration >25% LEL on 5-minute rolling average basis, description of whether floating roof was repaired/replaced/taken out of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records for gasoline cargo tank loading tests and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: For facilities subject to certain items in table 2 or § 63.11086(a)(6), keep records in hardcopy or electronic form of test results for each gasoline cargo tank loading for at least 5 years, covering annual certification testing (§ 63.11092(g)(1)) and periodic railcar bubble leak testing (§ 63.11092(g)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation must be kept up to date for each gasoline cargo tank loading and include at minimum: (i) name of test; (ii) cargo tank owner's name/address; (iii) cargo tank identification number; (iv) test location and date; (v) tester name/signature; (vi) witnessing inspector name/signature/affiliation if any; (vii) vapor tightness repair nature and timing; (viii) test results including tank capacity, test pressure, pressure/vacuum change (mm water), time period, number of leaks found, and leak definition. If following alternative § 63.11088(b), keep records documenting verification per Administrator requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment inventory records for gasoline service
rubrics_metrics.description: Each owner/operator subject to the equipment leak provisions shall prepare and maintain a record describing the types, identification numbers, and locations of all equipment in gasoline service. For facilities electing an instrument program under § 63.11089(b), include a full description of the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leak detection logbook entry requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For each leak detected under equipment leak inspections § 63.11089(b), record in the logbook the information specified in paragraphs (d)(1) through (7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required leak log entries: (1) equipment type and ID; (2) nature of leak (vapor or liquid) and detection method (sight, sound, smell); (3) date leak detected and date of each repair attempt; (4) repair methods applied in each attempt; (5) if repair not completed within 15 calendar days, record 'Repair delayed' and reason; (6) expected date of successful repair if not repaired within 15 days; (7) date of successful repair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leak inspection and detection recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators subject to § 63.11089(c) or § 60.503a(a)(2) shall maintain records of each leak inspection and leak identified as specified in paragraphs (e)(1) through (5) for at least 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records must indicate whether the inspection was under § 63.11089(c) or § 60.503a(a)(2), the leak determination method used. For Method 21 inspections, additionally keep date of inspection, inspector name, monitoring instrument ID, identification of equipment surveyed and instrument reading for each, date/time of instrument calibration and initials, calibration gas cylinder ID/certification date/certified concentration, instrument scale used, and daily calibration drift results. For OGI inspections, keep records specified in section 12 of appendix K to part 60. For each leak detected whether during inspection or routine duties, record equipment type and ID, detection date and person, nature of leak and detection method, date of each repair attempt and methods applied, date of successful repair and method of monitoring used to confirm repair (and if Method 21 used, maximum instrument reading; if OGI used, keep video footage), details for delayed repairs beyond 15 days including signatory, and for non-repairable leaks the maximum Method 21 reading, OGI video showing emissions, or signed record that leak still detectable by A/V/O methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous monitoring records for loading racks and storage vessels
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators subject to loading rack provisions or storage vessel provisions shall keep an up-to-date, readily accessible record of the continuous monitoring data required under § 63.11092(b) or (f). The record shall indicate time intervals during which gasoline cargo tank loadings occurred or may record operating parameter data only during such loadings; date/time of day shall be indicated at reasonable intervals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simultaneously with Notification of Compliance Status, report all data/calculations/engineering assessments/manufacturer's recommendations used to determine operating parameter values under § 63.11092(b) or (f). If using a flare under § 63.11(b) to comply with § 63.11087(a), include flare design and all VE readings, heat content determinations, flow rate measurements, and exit velocity determinations made during compliance determination. Keep an up-to-date copy of the monitoring and inspection plan required under § 63.11092(b)(1)(i)(B)(2) or (b)(1)(iii)(B)(2) and other specified records. If requesting approval to use vapor processing system or alternate operating parameter, submit description of planned reporting and recordkeeping procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMS/TOC CEMS/CPMS and thermal oxidation system monitoring records
rubrics_metrics.description: For each thermal oxidation system used to comply by monitoring combustion zone temperature, each pressure CPMS used to comply with § 60.502a(h), and each TOC CEMS used to comply, maintain specified records (applicable operating/emission limits, rolling averages, deviations, outages, calibration/inspection information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep: (i) applicable operating/emission limit for the CMS (including date ranges based on performance test); (ii) each 3-hour rolling average combustion zone temperature, each 5-minute average pressure CPMS reading, and each 3-hour rolling average TOC concentration (as propane); (iii) for each deviation of the 3-hour rolling avg temp limit, max loading pressure, or TOC concentration, record start date/time, duration, cause, and corrective action; (iv) for each CMS outage or out-of-control period, record start date/time, duration, cause, corrective action (for TOC CEMS outages using a limited alternative include indication of use of limited alternative); (v) each inspection or calibration including unique identifier, make/model, and date of calibration check; for TOC CEMS include type (FID, NDIR) and whether methane is excluded from reported TOC; (vi) for TOC CEMS outages using limited alternative, keep data for past 10 adsorption/desorption cycles and quantities while using alternative (vacuum pressure, purge gas quantities, durations, liquid product quantities); and (vii) other items specified in paragraph (g)(1)(vi) through (ix).

rubrics_metrics.name: Thermal oxidation/flare monitoring records and retention specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: For each thermal oxidation system used to comply with § 63.11092(e)(2)(ii) and for each flare used to comply with item 2 of table 3, maintain monitoring device outputs and visible emissions observations for specified retention periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain pilot flame monitoring device output for minimum 2 years, and retain records of each 15-minute block with at least one minute no pilot flame present when gasoline vapors were routed to the flare for minimum 5 years (identify start/end time/date of each 15-minute block). Retain visible emissions observation records per Method 22 for minimum 3 years, and if visible emissions observed more than 5 minutes in 2 consecutive hours but Method 22 not conducted for full 2-hour period, include estimates of cumulative minutes visible. Retain records of each 15-minute block period during which operating values are outside applicable operating limits when product is being loaded for at least 15 minutes, identifying the specific limit not met. Retain 15-minute block average cumulative flows and related pressure/temperature/molecular weight records and retention durations as specified (2 or 5 years depending on item). Retain component composition analyses and NHVvg analyzer data per specified retention periods and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of 5-minute time period loading records
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain records of all 5-minute time periods during which liquid product is loaded into gasoline cargo tanks or assumed to be loaded, and records of all 5-minute time periods when there was no liquid product loaded into gasoline cargo tanks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are required as part of monitoring and calculations for compliance and must be retained per applicable retention periods referenced elsewhere in the subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records of loadings without vapor tightness documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain records of each instance in which liquid product was loaded into a gasoline cargo tank for which vapor tightness documentation required under § 60.502(e)(1) or § 60.502a(e)(1) was not provided or available, for at least 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records shall include at minimum: cargo tank owner and address; cargo tank identification number; date/time of loading without documentation; date proper documentation was received or a statement that proper documentation was never received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records of non-submerged filling or improper connection incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep records for at least 5 years of each instance when liquid product was loaded into gasoline cargo tanks not using submerged filling, or not equipped with or not properly connected to vapor collection or balancing equipment compatible with the terminal/plant system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records must include at minimum: date/time of loading, type of deviation (e.g., not submerged filling, incompatible equipment, not properly connected), and cargo tank identification number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records for improperly connected plant vapor balancing events
rubrics_metrics.description: Bulk gasoline plants subject to § 63.11086(a)(6) must maintain records for at least 5 years of instances when gasoline was loaded between gasoline cargo tanks and storage tanks and the plant's vapor balancing system was not properly connected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include at minimum: date/time of gasoline loading not properly connected, cargo tank and storage tank identification numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deviation records for emissions limitations and work practice standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Each affected source shall keep records for each deviation of an emissions limitation (including operating limits), work practice standard, or O&M requirement in this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records must include: (1) date, start time, and duration of each deviation; (2) list of affected sources or equipment for each deviation, an estimate of quantity of each regulated pollutant emitted over any emission limit and description of the method used to estimate emissions; (3) actions taken to minimize emissions in accordance with § 63.11085(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Average gasoline throughput records
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators shall maintain records of the average gasoline throughput (in gallons per day) for at least 5 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of written procedures and performance evaluation plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep written procedures required under § 63.8(d)(2) on record for the life of the affected source or until it is no longer subject to the part; keep superseded versions of the performance evaluation plan on record and available for inspection for 5 years after each revision. Include the program of corrective action in the plan as required under § 63.8(d)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Records of performance tests/evaluations and submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep records of each performance test or performance evaluation conducted and each notification and report submitted to the Administrator for at least 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each performance test include an indication of whether liquid product loading is assumed to be loaded into a gasoline cargo tank or whether periods when no cargo tanks are being loaded are excluded in the determination of combustion zone temperature operating limit per § 60.503a(c)(8)(ii). If using the alternative in § 63.11092(h), for each performance test/evaluation include the pressure every 5 minutes while a cargo tank is being loaded and the highest instantaneous pressure during each loading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic records via CEDRI permitted but on-site access required
rubrics_metrics.description: Records required by this subpart that are submitted electronically via EPA's CEDRI may be maintained in electronic format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic maintenance does not affect the requirement to make records, data, and reports available upon request to a delegated authority or the EPA as part of an on-site compliance evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance test reporting timeline, content, and file format (post-November 4, 2024)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning November 4, 2024, within 60 days after completing each performance test, submit results following procedures in § 63.9(k). Include the combustion zone temperature operating parameter value set based on your performance test. If monitoring alternative § 63.11092(h) used, indicate use, identify each loading rack that loads gasoline cargo tanks, and report highest instantaneous pressure monitored during the test for each rack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data collected using EPA ERT-supported test methods must be submitted in an ERT-generated file format or an XML file consistent with the ERT schema. Data from test methods not supported by the ERT must be included as an attachment in the ERT or an alternate electronic file. Prior to Nov 4, 2024 follow § 63.13 reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance evaluation reporting timeline, content, and file format (post-November 4, 2024)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning November 4, 2024, within 60 days after completing each CEMS performance evaluation, submit results following § 63.9(k). If monitoring alternative § 63.11092(h) used, indicate use, identify loading racks, and report highest instantaneous pressure monitored during each identified loading rack's evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results of performance evaluations of CEMS measuring RATA pollutants that are supported by EPA's ERT must be submitted in ERT-generated file format or XML consistent with ERT schema. Results not supported by ERT must be included as an attachment in the ERT or alternate electronic file. Prior to Nov 4, 2024 follow § 63.13 reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semiannual compliance reporting requirements prior to May 8, 2027
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to May 8, 2027, owners/operators subject to control requirements shall include specified information in semiannual compliance reports to the Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include as applicable: (i) for storage vessels, information per § 60.115b(a),(b),(c) or § 63.1066 depending on control option; (ii) for loading racks, each loading of a gasoline cargo tank for which vapor tightness documentation had not previously been obtained by the facility; (iii) for equipment leak inspections, number of equipment leaks not repaired within 15 days after detection; (iv) for storage vessels complying with § 63.11087(b) after Jan 10, 2011, NOCS info may be included in next semiannual report in lieu of separate NOCS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess emissions reporting requirements (prior to May 8, 2027)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each owner/operator subject to control requirements shall submit an excess emissions report to the Administrator at the time the semiannual compliance report is submitted, including specified information for excess emissions events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: (i) each instance of non-vapor-tight cargo tank loading where owner/operator failed to ensure cargo tank would not be reloaded before vapor tightness documentation obtained; (ii) each reloading of a non-vapor-tight cargo tank before documentation obtained in accordance with § 63.11094(b); (iii) each exceedance or failure to maintain monitored operating parameter value determined under § 63.11092(b) with monitoring data for days and description/timing of steps taken to repair or maintain vapor collection/processing systems or CMS; (v) for each occurrence of equipment leak with no repair attempt within 5 days or repair not completed within 15 days, include date leak detected, date of each repair attempt, reasons for delay, and date of successful repair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semiannual reporting requirements on/after May 8, 2027 — facility identification and certifier statement
rubrics_metrics.description: On or after May 8, 2027, submit semiannual reports with specified general facility information and a certifying statement by a responsible official, following the procedure in paragraph (e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required general facility information: facility name; physical address (city, county, State); latitude/longitude in decimal degrees with at least five decimal places; contact person name, mailing address, telephone, email; type of facility (categories listed); date of report and reporting period (no date required if submitted via CEDRI); statement by a responsible official with name, title, and signature (electronic signature via CEDRI replaces physical signature).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting CMS deviations in semiannual reports (on/after May 8, 2027)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each thermal oxidation system, pressure CPMS, and TOC CEMS, report instances when monitored values were outside established operating limits during liquid product loading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each instance report: (A) date and start time of the deviation; (B) duration of the deviation in hours; (C) each 3-hour rolling average combustion zone temperature, average pressure, or 3-hour rolling average TOC concentration during the deviation.
